title: A Small Word Steals the Victory Speech
summary:
Abdul El-Sayed has won a Senate seat in Michigan. He will be the first Muslim American U.S. senator. His parents came from Egypt.

At his victory party in Detroit on November 4, El-Sayed said a funny hello to Vice President JD Vance. He said, 'JD, habibi.' The word 'habibi' means 'my beloved' in Arabic. In everyday talk, it is more like 'buddy,' 'pal,' or 'bro.' Fans wore shirts that said 'Habibi for Abdul.'

During the race, Vance had warned that El-Sayed would lead rioters in burning down Detroit. El-Sayed joked that Vance must still swear him in as a senator in January. He also said his campaign turned 'inshallah,' or 'God willing,' into 'hamdulillah,' or 'thank God.'

People online shared music clips with the word 'habibi.' Egyptian scholar Khalil al-Anani called it the sweetest word and thanked El-Sayed for bringing joy to Egyptians.

El-Sayed had faced harsh words during the race. President Donald Trump called him a 'jihadist,' brought up the September 11 attacks, and kept saying his name wrong. El-Sayed joked back that Trump can just call him 'senator.'
why_it_matters: It shows kids that words from their family's language can be shared with pride and bring joy to others.

keywords.explanation: The Senate is a group of lawmakers who help make laws for the United States.
A campaign is all the work a person does to try to win an election.
Rioters are people in a crowd who act in a wild and violent way.
A scholar is a person who has studied a subject for a long time and knows a lot about it.
It is a harsh word for a person who uses violence in the name of a strict form of Islam.

A seat on the Detroit city council
The job of governor of Michigan

background_read: A senator is one of the people voters choose to help make laws for the whole country in Washington, D.C.
When a candidate wins an election, they often give a victory speech to thank their supporters and share their hopes for the job ahead.
Habibi is a warm Arabic word that means my beloved, and friends often use it the way English speakers use buddy, pal, or bro.
Article_Structure: WHO: Abdul El-Sayed, who will be the first Muslim American U.S. senator, and Vice President JD Vance.
WHAT: El-Sayed won a Senate seat in Michigan and greeted Vance with 'JD, habibi' at his victory party.
WHERE: Detroit, Michigan, where El-Sayed held his victory party on November 4.
WHY: El-Sayed used humor and the Arabic word 'habibi' to answer the harsh warnings and name-calling he faced during the race.
